Solution 3 reaches the answer I believe is correct, 1/(2t(t−1)). I checked its upper bound and the counting behind the matching construction, but I did not verify the even-q case or the near-complete coverage of pairs in detail.

**Solution 3.** Take a copy of K_{t,t} with sides A and B, and two vertices u, v in A. Then B lies in N(u)∩N(v). Since K_{2,t+1}-freeness caps this set at t vertices, B = N(u)∩N(v). The same argument applies to pairs in B, so every pair of vertices is a same-side pair of at most one copy. Each copy has t(t−1) same-side pairs, which gives the upper bound n²/(2t(t−1)).

The construction is norm-graph-like on n = t^{2e−1} vertices, and the claim that almost all pairs are covered by a copy is plausible. It would give a matching lower bound, so the limit is 1/(2t(t−1)). The construction handles even t only by an unspecified "analogous" version, so that part is not checked.

**Solution 1.** Its answer 1/t! is not supported. The argument is heuristic and does not match the pair-counting upper bound, so it is rejected.

**Solution 2.** Its key step is wrong. The t-subsets of N(v) pairwise meet in at most one vertex, but that allows on the order of deg(v)² such sets, not O(deg(v)). The O(n^{3/2}) bound on copies therefore fails, and the limit 0 contradicts the construction in Solution 3.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: ACCEPT
